title: Real conversations
goal: Hold long, natural conversations — catching up with an old friend, getting through a family dinner, arguing about where to go and planning a trip — linking ideas in long sentences and switching between तू, तुम्ही and आपण as you go.
intro:
This is where everything comes together. Real conversations don't come in neat units: at one Pune family dinner you'll call your grandmother **तुम्ही**, your cousin **तू**, dodge an aunt's question about marriage, argue about Goa versus the Konkan, and settle the trip — all in twenty minutes.

This last unit gives you the glue for long, flowing speech: **जरी… तरी** 'although', **शिवाय** 'besides', **-आवं म्हणून** 'so that', **थोडक्यात** 'in short' and the very Marathi **असो** 'anyway'. It shows you how to switch register mid-conversation, how to take the floor and get back to your point, and how to wrap things up the way Marathi speakers do. Then it's over to you: आता फक्त बोलत राहा!

grammar.title: Linking long sentences
grammar.body:
To speak in long, flowing sentences you need a handful of linkers on top of आणि, पण, कारण, म्हणून and त्यामुळे.

**Although: जरी… तरी…** — a correlative pair like जो… तो: **जरी** पाऊस होता, **तरी** आम्ही गेलो 'although it was raining, we went'. जरी can be dropped, तरी can't: पाऊस होता, तरी गेलो. With a participle you can also say **-ऊनसुद्धा**: पाऊस असूनसुद्धा गेलो.

**Besides / not only that**: **शिवाय** 'besides, what's more': स्वस्त आहे, **शिवाय** जवळ आहे. Stronger: **एवढंच नाही तर…** 'not only that, but…'.

**So that / so as not to**: optative -आवं + **म्हणून**: तुला कळा**वं म्हणून** सांगतोय 'I'm telling you so that you know'; -ऊ **नये म्हणून** 'so as not to': ट्रेन चुकू **नये म्हणून** लवकर निघालो. (Formal: जेणेकरून.)

**At least**: **निदान … तरी**: निदान फोन तरी करायचास! 'you could at least have called!'

**In short / anyway**: **थोडक्यात** 'in short' sums up; **असो** 'anyway' closes a topic and moves on.

A long Marathi sentence often chains -ऊन participles and finishes with a single verb: सकाळी लवकर उठून, आवरून, घाटातून ड्राइव्ह करून आम्ही दुपारी पोहोचलो.

examples.en: Although I was tired, I went to the party. (man)

grammar.title: Switching register mid-conversation
grammar.body:
At a family dinner you switch register several times a minute, and the verb has to switch with you.

**Elders** — grandparents, uncles and aunts, parents' friends, in-laws: **तुम्ही**, plural verbs (बसा, आलात, घ्या), **अहो** to get their attention, and the respectful plural when you talk *about* them: आजी बरोबर बोलत**ायत**, काका आले **आहेत**.

**Siblings, cousins, friends**: **तू**, with ए / अरे / अगं: ए दादा, तू जरा पाणी **आण** ना.

**Parents**: in most modern families **आई** gets **तू**; **बाबा** gets तू in some families and तुम्ही in others — follow what the family does.

**Elders to you**: always तू, often with **बाळा**, **राजा**, **गं / रे**, and sentence-final **हो** for emphasis: सावकाश जा **हो**.

**आपण** has two jobs: very formal 'you' (announcements, customer care, a speech) and, far more often, inclusive 'we' (you and I): **आपण** सगळे मिळून जाऊ.

What changes when you switch: imperatives (बस → बसा, आण → आणा), present (येतोस → येता), past (आलास → आलात, केलंस → केलंत), future (करशील → कराल). One sentence can contain both: आजोबा, **तुम्ही बसा**; ए राहुल, **तू** ताट **घे**.

The trap: switching to तू with an elder sounds rude, but staying with तुम्ही with a close friend sounds cold — and if someone older says **मला तू म्हण** 'call me तू', it's a compliment, so do it.

examples.native: आजोबा, तुम्ही बसा, मी पाणी आणतो.
examples.roman: ādzobā, tumhī basā, mī pāṇī āṇto.
examples.en: Grandpa, you sit down, I'll get the water. (man)

examples.roman: āī, tū paṇ bas nā ātā.
examples.en: Mum, you sit down too now.

grammar.title: Holding the floor, moving on and wrapping up
grammar.body:
**Taking the floor**: **एक मिनिट**, **माझं ऐक / ऐका**, **मुद्दा असा आहे की…** 'the point is…', **मी काय म्हणतो / म्हणते…** 'here's what I think…'.

**Keeping it**: **आणि हो…** 'oh, and…', **अजून एक…** 'one more thing…', **म्हणजे बघ…** 'I mean, look…'.

**Getting back to your point**: **हां, तर मी काय सांगत होतो / होते…** 'so, as I was saying…'.

**Moving on or letting go**: **असो** 'anyway', **जाऊ दे** 'forget it', **ते सोड** 'leave that'.

**Agreeing a plan**: **मग फायनल?** → **ठरलं तर!**; giving in: **ठीक आहे, तुझी मर्जी**.

**Wrapping up**: **थोडक्यात**, **बाकीचं नंतर बोलू**, **चला, निघतो / निघते**, **संपर्कात राहा**, and finally **येतो / येते** — Marathi speakers say 'I'll come' rather than 'I'm going' when they leave, because जातो sounds like you won't be back. Goodbyes are long: expect two or three rounds of चला… बरं… येतो! at the door.

examples.en: Just a minute — listen to me.

examples.native: मी काय म्हणते, आपण गोव्याऐवजी कोकणात जाऊ.
examples.roman: mī kāy mhaṇte, āpaṇ govyāaivajī koṅkaṇāt dzāū.
examples.en: Here's what I think: let's go to the Konkan instead of Goa. (woman)

examples.native: हां, तर मी काय सांगत होतो…
examples.roman: hāṃ, tar mī kāy sāṅgat hoto…

examples.native: चला, निघते मी, बाकीचं नंतर बोलू.
examples.roman: tsalā, nighte mī, bākītsaṃ nantar bolū.
examples.en: Right, I'm off — we'll talk about the rest later. (woman)

dialogue.title: Sunday dinner in Kothrud
dialogue.setting: Sunday dinner at the family home in Kothrud, Pune: Ketaki (28), her mother, her grandmother (Aaji) and her cousin Rohan.

lines.speaker: Aai
lines.native: चला, जेवायला बसा! जेवण गार होतंय.
lines.roman: tsalā, jevāylā basā! jevaṇ gār hotaṃy.
lines.en: Come on, sit down to eat! The food's getting cold.

lines.speaker: Ketaki
lines.native: आजी, तुम्ही इथे बसा, मी वाढते.
lines.roman: ādzī, tumhī ithe basā, mī vāḍhte.
lines.en: Aaji, you sit here, I'll serve.

lines.speaker: Aaji
lines.native: बस गं, तू पण बस. मग केतकी, लग्नाचं काय ठरवलंस?
lines.roman: bas gaṃ, tū paṇ bas. mag ketakī, lagnātsaṃ kāy ṭharavlaṃs?
lines.en: Sit, sit, you sit down too. So, Ketaki, what have you decided about getting married?

lines.speaker: Ketaki
lines.native: आजी, प्लीज, पुन्हा तोच विषय नको.
lines.roman: ādzī, plīz, punhā tots viṣay nako.
lines.en: Aaji, please, not that topic again.

lines.speaker: Aai
lines.native: आजी बरोबर बोलतायत. एक चांगलं स्थळ आलंय, मुलगा इंजिनीअर आहे, शिवाय पुण्यातच आहे.
lines.roman: ādzī barobar boltāyat. ek tsāṅglaṃ sthaḷ ālaṃy, mulgā iñjinīar āhe, shivāy puṇyāts āhe.
lines.en: Aaji's right. A good proposal has come — the boy's an engineer, and what's more, he's right here in Pune.

lines.speaker: Ketaki
lines.native: आई, माझं ऐकून तर घे! मुद्दा असा आहे की मला आधी करिअरमध्ये सेटल व्हायचं आहे.
lines.roman: āī, mādzhaṃ aikūn tar ghe! muddā asā āhe kī malā ādhī kariarmadhye seṭal vhāytsaṃ āhe.
lines.en: Mum, at least hear me out! The thing is, I want to get settled in my career first.

lines.speaker: Rohan
lines.native: असो! केतकी, आपला कोकणाचा बेत फायनल ना?
lines.roman: aso! ketakī, āplā koṅkaṇātsā bet fāynal nā?
lines.en: Anyway! Ketaki, our Konkan trip is final, right?

lines.speaker: Ketaki
lines.native: हो! जरी सगळ्यांच्या तारखा जुळत नव्हत्या, तरी शेवटी पुढचा शनिवार ठरला.
lines.roman: ho! dzarī sagḷyānchyā tārkhā dzuḷat navhtyā, tarī shevaṭī puḍhtsā shanivār ṭharlā.
lines.en: Yes! Even though nobody's dates matched, in the end we fixed next Saturday.

lines.speaker: Aaji
lines.native: कोकणात? पावसात घाटातून? सावकाश जा हो.
lines.roman: koṅkaṇāt? pāvsāt ghāṭātūn? sāvkāsh dzā ho.
lines.en: To the Konkan? Through the ghat in the rain? Do drive carefully.

lines.speaker: Rohan
lines.native: काळजी करू नका आजी, मी ड्राइव्ह करणार आहे.
lines.roman: kāḷjī karū nakā ādzī, mī ḍrāivh karṇār āhe.
lines.en: Don't worry, Aaji, I'll be driving.

lines.speaker: Aai
lines.native: पुरे दोघं! आधी जेवा, बाकीचं नंतर बोलू.
lines.roman: pure doghaṃ! ādhī jevā, bākītsaṃ nantar bolū.
lines.en: That's enough, you two! Eat first, we'll talk about the rest later.

lines.speaker: Aaji
lines.native: आणि केतकी, लग्नाचा विषय संपलेला नाहीये हं!
lines.roman: āṇi ketakī, lagnātsā viṣay samplelā nāhīye haṃ!
lines.en: And Ketaki — the marriage topic isn't over, mind you!

culture:
Family meals are where Marathi is really spoken: several generations at one table, each addressed differently, food pressed on you with **आग्रह**, and an aunt's **टोमणा** about your weight, your job or your marriage plans served with the dal. The marriage question — **लग्नाचं काय?** — is a running joke among young Maharashtrians; the trick is to deflect with humour (**योग्य वेळ आली की सांगेन** 'I'll tell you when the time is right') or let a cousin change the subject with a well-timed **असो!**

Weekend trips are a Pune and Mumbai obsession, especially in the monsoon: down the ghats to the Konkan coast (Alibag, Dapoli, Ganpatipule), up to Lonavala and Mahabaleshwar, or a fort trek in the Sahyadris. Planning one in a WhatsApp group — dates that won't match, a budget per head, homestay or hotel — is a conversation you'll have many times. And when it's finally time to leave, remember that Marathi speakers say **येतो / येते** ('I'll come'), never a bare जातो, and that a proper goodbye takes at least three rounds at the door. **आता तुमची पाळी — मराठीत बोलत राहा!**

lessons.title: Although, besides, so that

tip.title: जरी… तरी, शिवाय, म्हणून — linking ideas
tip.body:
- 'Although': **जरी** …, **तरी** …: जरी उशीर झाला, तरी आलो.
- 'Besides, what's more': **शिवाय**.
- 'So that': -आवं **म्हणून**; 'so as not to': -ऊ **नये म्हणून**.
- 'At least': **निदान … तरी**; 'in short': **थोडक्यात**.

new: जरी पटलं नाही, तरी ऐकून घे.

lessons.title: Family dinner

tip.title: तू, तुम्ही — switching as you go
tip.body:
- Elders (आजी-आजोबा, काका-काकू, in-laws): **तुम्ही**, plural verbs, **अहो** to call them.
- Siblings, cousins, friends: **तू**, with ए / अरे / अगं.
- आई usually gets **तू**; बाबा depends on the family.
- The verb switches too: बस → **बसा**, आण → **आणा**, आलास → **आलात**.
tip.pattern: आजी, तुम्ही बसा  ·  ए दादा, तू बस

new: आई, प्लीज, पुन्हा तोच विषय नको.

sentences.native: आजी, तुम्ही बसा, मी वाढते.
sentences.roman: ādzī, tumhī basā, mī vāḍhte.
sentences.en: Grandma, you sit down, I'll serve. (woman)

sentences.native: ए दादा, तू जरा पाणी आण ना.
sentences.roman: e dādā, tū dzarā pāṇī āṇ nā.
sentences.en: Hey, bro, get some water, will you?

sentences.native: काका, तुम्ही कधी आलात?
sentences.roman: kākā, tumhī kadhī ālāt?
sentences.en: Uncle, when did you get here?

sentences.native: माझा चुलत भाऊ अमेरिकेत असतो.
sentences.roman: mādzhā tsulat bhāū ameriket asto.
sentences.en: My cousin lives in America.

sentences.native: आत्याने परत लग्नावरून टोमणा मारला.
sentences.roman: ātyāne parat lagnāvarūn ṭomṇā mārlā.
sentences.en: My aunt made another dig about marriage.

sentences.native: आईला एक नवीन स्थळ आलंय म्हणे.
sentences.roman: āīlā ek navīn sthaḷ ālaṃy mhaṇe.
sentences.en: Apparently Mum's had a new marriage proposal (for me).

sentences.native: वडीलधाऱ्यांशी बोलताना मान ठेवायचा.
sentences.roman: vaḍīldhāryānshī boltānā mān ṭhevāytsā.
sentences.en: You show respect when you talk to your elders.

sentences.native: इतकं औपचारिक बोलू नकोस, तू म्हण मला.
sentences.roman: itkaṃ aupchārik bolū nakos, tū mhaṇ malā.
sentences.en: Don't be so formal — call me तू.

sentences.native: आमची सून खूप गोड आहे.
sentences.roman: āmchī sūn khūp goḍ āhe.
sentences.en: Our daughter-in-law is a sweetheart.

sentences.native: जेवण गार होतंय, आधी जेवा, मग बोलू.
sentences.roman: jevaṇ gār hotaṃy, ādhī jevā, mag bolū.
sentences.en: The food's getting cold — eat first, then we'll talk.

tip.title: Holding the floor — and letting go
tip.body:
- Take the floor: **एक मिनिट**, **माझं ऐक**, **मुद्दा असा आहे की…**, **मी काय म्हणतो…**
- Get back to it: **हां, तर मी काय सांगत होतो…**
- Move on: **असो**, **जाऊ दे**.
- Give in: **ठीक आहे, तुझी मर्जी**.

sentences.native: एक मिनिट, आधी माझं ऐकून तर घे!
sentences.roman: ek miniṭ, ādhī mādzhaṃ aikūn tar ghe!
sentences.en: Hang on — at least hear me out first!

sentences.native: मुद्दा असा आहे की गोव्यात डिसेंबरमध्ये खूप गर्दी असते.
sentences.roman: muddā asā āhe kī govyāt ḍisembarmadhye khūp gardī aste.
sentences.en: The thing is, Goa's really crowded in December.

sentences.native: मी काय म्हणतो, आपण यावेळी कोकणात जाऊ.
sentences.roman: mī kāy mhaṇto, āpaṇ yāveḷī koṅkaṇāt dzāū.
sentences.en: Here's what I think: let's go to the Konkan this time. (man)

sentences.native: मला गोवा पसंत नाही असं नाही, पण…
sentences.roman: malā govā pasant nāhī asaṃ nāhī, paṇ…
sentences.en: It's not that I don't like Goa, but…

sentences.native: तिला मनवणं सोपं नाही.
sentences.roman: tilā manavṇaṃ sopaṃ nāhī.
sentences.en: She's not easy to talk round.

sentences.native: शेवटी मी सगळ्यांना मनवलं.
sentences.roman: shevaṭī mī sagḷyānnā manavlaṃ.
sentences.en: In the end I talked everyone round.

sentences.native: असो, जाऊ दे, तुम्ही ठरवा.
sentences.roman: aso, dzāū de, tumhī ṭharvā.
sentences.en: Anyway, never mind — you lot decide.

sentences.native: ठीक आहे, तुझी मर्जी, पण नंतर तक्रार करायची नाही!
sentences.roman: ṭhīk āhe, tudzhī mardzī, paṇ nantar takrār karāychī nāhī!
sentences.en: OK, have it your way — but no complaining later!

sentences.native: हां, तर मी काय सांगत होते…
sentences.roman: hāṃ, tar mī kāy sāṅgat hote…
sentences.en: So, as I was saying… (woman)

sentences.native: या पावसाळ्यात कोकणाचा बेत आहे.
sentences.roman: yā pāvsāḷyāt koṅkaṇātsā bet āhe.
sentences.en: We're planning a Konkan trip this monsoon.

sentences.native: बजेट प्रत्येकी पाच हजार, बरोबर?
sentences.roman: bajeṭ pratyekī pāts hadzār, barobar?
sentences.en: The budget is five thousand each, right?

sentences.native: हॉटेलपेक्षा होमस्टे बरा, घरचं जेवण मिळतं.
sentences.roman: hôṭelpekṣā homsṭe barā, ghartsaṃ jevaṇ miḷtaṃ.
sentences.en: A homestay's better than a hotel — you get home-cooked food.

sentences.native: घाटातून ड्राइव्ह करताना जाम मजा येते.
sentences.roman: ghāṭātūn ḍrāivh kartānā dzām madzā yete.
sentences.en: Driving down the ghat is super fun.

sentences.native: राहण्याची सोय झाली का?
sentences.roman: rāhṇyāchī soy dzhālī kā?
sentences.en: Have we sorted out somewhere to stay?

sentences.native: सगळ्यांच्या तारखा जुळत नाहीयेत.
sentences.roman: sagḷyānchyā tārkhā dzuḷat nāhīyet.
sentences.en: Nobody's dates match.

sentences.native: शुक्रवारी रात्री निघू, म्हणजे शनिवार पूर्ण मिळेल.
sentences.roman: shukravārī rātrī nighū, mhaṇje shanivār pūrṇa miḷel.
sentences.en: Let's leave Friday night, so we get the whole of Saturday.

sentences.native: मग फायनल? शुक्रवारी रात्री दहा वाजता.
sentences.roman: mag fāynal? shukravārī rātrī dahā vādztā.
sentences.en: So it's final? Friday night at ten.

sentences.native: ठरलं तर! मी ग्रुपवर टाकतो.
sentences.roman: ṭharlaṃ tar! mī grupvar ṭākto.
sentences.en: Done, then! I'll post it on the group. (man)

lessons.title: Wrapping up and staying in touch

sentences.native: चला, उशीर झाला, बाकीचं नंतर बोलू.
sentences.roman: tsalā, ushīr dzhālā, bākītsaṃ nantar bolū.
sentences.en: Right, it's late — let's talk about the rest later.

sentences.native: संपर्कात राहा, आणि पुढच्या वेळी आमच्याकडे या.
sentences.roman: samparkāt rāhā, āṇi puḍhchyā veḷī āmchyākaḍe yā.
sentences.en: Stay in touch, and come to our place next time.

sentences.native: आपला संपर्क तुटला होता, आता परत भेटत राहू.
sentences.roman: āplā samparka tuṭlā hotā, ātā parat bheṭat rāhū.
sentences.en: We'd lost touch — let's keep meeting from now on.

sentences.native: आरामात जा, पोहोचल्यावर मेसेज कर.
sentences.roman: ārāmāt dzā, pohotslyāvar mesej kar.
sentences.en: Go carefully, and message me when you get there.

sentences.native: पुढच्या वेळी आरामात भेटू, घाई न करता.
sentences.roman: puḍhchyā veḷī ārāmāt bheṭū, ghāī na kartā.
sentences.en: Next time let's meet properly, without rushing.

sentences.native: थोडक्यात सांगायचं तर, ट्रिप भन्नाट झाली!
sentences.roman: thoḍkyāt sāṅgāytsaṃ tar, ṭrip bhannāṭ dzhālī!
sentences.en: To cut a long story short, the trip was amazing!

sentences.native: असो, तू कधी येतोयस पुण्याला?
sentences.roman: aso, tū kadhī yetoys puṇyālā?
sentences.en: Anyway, when are you coming to Pune?

sentences.native: खूप छान वाटलं भेटून. चला, येतो!
sentences.roman: khūp chhān vāṭlaṃ bheṭūn. tsalā, yeto!
sentences.en: It was so nice to see you. Right, I'll be off! (man)
